question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` allow scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if so what exact wildcard grammar is acceptable for Gateway browser-origin authorization?
rationale: The request changes which browser origins can reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket handling, and current docs intentionally describe full-origin allowlisting plus the global `*` as the only wildcard policy.

options.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
options.body: Define a small allowed grammar, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allowed and rejected cases before accepting the feature.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for deliberately broad local testing.

options.title: Defer to broader pattern design
options.body: Wait for the loopback origin-pattern work to settle and then decide whether Chrome extension wildcards belong in the same contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
recommendation.body: Define a small allowed grammar, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allowed and rejected cases before accepting the feature.
